candidates.abstract: Single cell transcriptomic profiling of the retina provided important insights into the genetic signals in retinal cells that enable vision. However, conventional 3’ short-read sequencing method is not suitable to identify isoform variants. Here we utilized Iso-Seq with full-length sequencing to profile the human retina at single cell resolution for isoform discovery. We generated a retina transcriptome dataset consisting of 23,523 nuclei from three donor retina, and identified 15,967 known isoforms and 7,617 novel isoforms across 10 major cell types. We showed that up to 2.6% of genes utilized multiple promoters across major retinal cell types. Also, our results identified novel transcript variants for inherited retinal disease (IRD) genes and differential usage of exon splicing in major retinal cell types. Altogether, this study reported a detailed Human Retina Gene Atlas to study isoform diversity at single cell resolution, providing an expanded view of the complex transcriptomic landscape in the retina. Iso-Seq enabled isoform discovery of human retina at single cell levels. This study revealed novel isoforms, splice junctions and alternative promoters across major retinal cell types, providing insights into the retinal transcriptomic landscape.

candidates.title: Promoted phase transition in perovskite heterojunctions via in-situ regulated 2D intermediates enables stable solar cells
candidates.authors: Shengli Yue, Guanghan Zhao, Weichuan Zhang, Shuai You, Wanfei Shi, Rongshen Yang, Weichao Zhang, Tinghuan Yang, Shilin Li, Hong Zhang, Yu Chen, Chenglin Yang, Xiaopeng Zheng, Kui Zhao, Huiying Hao, Haibo Mao, Changli Ma, He Cheng, Nam-Gyu Park, Yuan Zhang, Huiqiong Zhou
candidates.abstract: The formation of 2D/3D perovskite heterojunctions often relies on spacer-induced ion-exchange, which is difficult to achieve graded distribution of 2D species for efficient charge transport. Here, we report a phase-regulation strategy for formamidinium-based perovskites guided by pre-adding a full-composition 2D perovskite (hereinafter denoted as Pre-2D) into the FA-based 3D perovskite precursor. This approach enables coordinated control of precursor organization and interfacial phase evolution, resulting in bottom-up growth of phase-stable α‑FAPbI3 with vertically aligned 2D/3D heterostructures. The gradient architecture at the buried interface improves crystallographic orientation, suppresses defect-assisted recombination, and mitigates ion migration. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.61% at room temperature with a high efficiency of 28.01% at 245 K, and 23.58% for mini-modules. Notably, devices retain over 95% of initial efficiency after 1100 hours of continuous MPP tracking and 1700 hours of damp-heat testing. These findings provide a scalable route to regulate phase competition and buried-interface energetics in FA-based perovskites, advancing the development of efficient and durable perovskite photovoltaics. Efficient perovskite solar cells require graded layered junctions, yet spacer-driven ion exchange offers poor control. Yue et al. added a preformed layered perovskite to direct vertical phase growth at the buried interface, improving efficiency, stability, and module scalability.

candidates.authors: Hui-Ru Liu, Chun-Lin Song, Peng-Fei Jia, Yu Luo, Rui-Yang Wang, De-li Wang, Jeremy D. Murray, Hai-Feng Wang, Wei-Cai Yang
candidates.abstract: The root nodules of leguminous plants contain rhizobia that proliferate and differentiate into bacteroids inside symbiosomes for nitrogen fixation. Hosts must tightly regulate rhizobial proliferation to optimize symbiotic benefits and avoid pathogenicity, yet the mechanisms governing this balancing act remain unknown for most legumes. Here, using in vitro assays and pectin-deficient mutants, we show that intracellular demethylesterified pectin (DMEP) directly constrains rhizobial growth in soybean nodules. Furthermore, we show that host factors HOF1 and HOF2 act as regulators of DMEP stability, binding DMEP to prevent its degradation via polygalacturonase. Genetically altered plants with modestly reduced rhizobial abundance exhibited significantly higher nitrogenase activity per gram of nodules, revealing the importance of host-mediated restriction of bacterial numbers in determining symbiotic efficiency. Our findings uncover an unanticipated role for cell wall components in controlling endosymbiont population size and provide insights into host–symbiont interactions, with potential implications for legume improvement and crop yields. candidates.title: Bacteria-induced TLR2 signaling unleashes multiple mechanisms to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance cancer immunity
candidates.authors: Timothy F. Campbell, Jesse Garcia Castillo, Sebastian Fernandez, Ola Mostafa, Diego Gonzalez Ventura, Jenna Vickery, Stefan Homentcovschi, Nicole Flores Hernandez, Julia Ybarra, Daniel A. Portnoy, Michel DuPage
candidates.abstract: Abstract Toll-like receptors (TLRs) support T cell priming in lymphatic tissues, but whether TLR stimulation within tumors also affects T cell function locally remains undefined. Here, we show that TLR2 signaling is necessary to promote CD8 + T cell-mediated tumor control by dual intravenous and intratumoral delivery of attenuated Listeria monocytogenes (IV + IT Lm ). TLR2 signaling supports T cell priming in the spleen during IV infection, but unexpectedly, TLR2 is also critical for the activity of anti- Lm CD8 + T cells in tumors upon IT Lm injection. TLR2 signaling is unique among all TLRs in its capacity to drive a cDC2-dependent reduction in regulatory T cells (Treg) and destabilize Foxp3 expression. TLR2-mediated Treg destabilization correlates with increased tumor antigen cross-presentation and stronger antitumor CD8 + T cell responses. Ultimately, TLR2-dependent Treg depletion is required for tumor control by IV + IT Lm . These findings reveal a novel role for TLR2 activation by bacteria in tumors to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance tumor-specific T cell responses.

candidates.title: Dissecting the root-fungal interface in 3D reveals spatially distinct signalling landscapes
candidates.authors: Syona Baptista Thomas, M Sreepadmanabh, Vidha Srivastava, Abhirami Puzhakkal, Tapomoy Bhattacharjee, Amey Redkar
candidates.abstract: Plant-fungal interactions in the rhizosphere influence plant health. Current understanding of these processes largely derives from in vitro flat plates, hydroponics and gnotobiotic platforms. However, fungal-plant interactions largely occur in soil – a disordered and granular 3D environment with heterogeneous elasto-viscoplastic properties – whose inherent opacity precludes direct visualisation of the infection. How the physical structure of such natural habitats influences interkingdom interactions remains unknown. Here, we introduce an optically transparent 3D jammed granular microgel matrix that mimics the mechanical properties of natural microenvironments. This platform supports long-term co-culture of plants and fungi, while being compatible with classical physiological assays. We accomplish a direct cellular-level visualisation of the plant-fungal interface. Specifically, host-derived signals prior to the physical contact trigger hyphal reorientation towards the root tips. Using spatiotemporally resolved transcriptomics we discover distinct pathogen-host ex- and in-planta signalling modules, which are associated with granular heterogeneous environments. Together, our findings establish an experimental platform for dissecting fungal development and pathogenesis with unprecedented microscopic and molecular resolution. Plant-fungal interactions in the rhizosphere influence plant health. Here the authors describe an optically transparent granular microgel matrix that mimics the mechanical properties of natural microenvironments to dissect fungal development and pathogenesis.

candidates.title: Single-molecule landscape of DNA replication pausing
candidates.authors: Sathish Thiyagarajan, Anna M. Rogers, Carolin A. Müller, Conrad A. Nieduszynski
candidates.abstract: Abstract A pause in DNA synthesis that occurs when the replisome encounters an obstacle could lead to genome instability. Although important, systematic identification of replication pause sites is challenging due to their low frequency and delocalised nature. Here we present a single-molecule identification of sites of replisome perturbation across a eukaryotic genome using long-read nanopore sequencing. For each single-molecule replication pause we determine the direction of replication, leading/lagging-strand identity, location and approximate duration, and whether the replisome resumed synthesis. Although pauses are largely diffuse over the genome, they are significantly enriched over transcribed features and correlate with transcription and R-loop levels. Transcription-replication conflicts are more numerous when head-on than co-directional. Finally, we identify genomic loci with a strong bias towards leading over lagging strand pauses, consistent with uncoupling of the helicase from polymerase epsilon. As one such locus overlaps with an epigenetically-regulated gene, we suggest that helicase-polymerase uncoupling resulting from replication pausing could trigger epigenetic switching.

candidates.title: Global intercomparison of ocean-based geochemical carbon dioxide removal efficiencies
candidates.authors: Mengyang Zhou, Mary-Louise Timmermans, Elizabeth Yankovsky, Michael D. Tyka, Matthew C. Long
candidates.abstract: Abstract Ocean-based geochemical CO 2 removal approaches, including ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) and direct ocean removal (DOR), have received attention for their potential to remove billion-ton-scale amounts of CO 2 from the atmosphere. Their viability at scale depends on efficiency. Here, we develop a unified framework for evaluating the efficiencies of ocean geochemical perturbations: OAE adds alkalinity, DOR removes dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), and combined alkalinity and DIC addition (ADA) adds both simultaneously. Using a global ocean biogeochemical model, we map global and seasonal DOR efficiency and compare it with OAE efficiency. Further, we show that OAE and DOR simulations can be combined to quantify the effect of simultaneous perturbations in alkalinity and DIC. This enables direct quantification of the oceanic fate of ADA perturbations from approaches such as enhanced rock weathering, riverine alkalinity enhancement and accelerated weathering of limestone. In these approaches, the added alkalinity partially equilibrates with CO 2 before entering the ocean, effectively adding both alkalinity and DIC.

candidates.title: Unidirectional rolling of single-crystal graphene into nanoscrolls
candidates.authors: Sheng Li, Shining Xu, Jiayi Hu, Weichuan Chen, Menglan Li, Zheng Wei, Tianqi Bai, Shiwei Wang, Jiaxin Shao, Qimeng Zhang, Fangfang Li, Yunsong Ge, Guangcun Gao, Bo Jin, Bo Yang, Li Lin, Peng Gao, Jian Zhang, Qing Chen, Jianbo Yin, Xiucai Sun, Kaicheng Jia, Zhongfan Liu
candidates.abstract: Transforming planar two-dimensional (2D) materials into rolled-up nanoscrolls has attracted broad interest, owing to the introduction of new degrees of freedom for materials design and property modulation. As one of the most representative 2D materials, graphene is a promising candidate for nanoscroll fabrication. However, the practical exploitation of graphene nanoscrolls has been hindered by the lack of reliable methods for precise control over structure and orientation, limiting their integration into large-scale electronics and optoelectronics. Here we show the aligned fabrication of graphene nanoscrolls via deterministic rolling of wafer-scale single-crystal graphene films during post-growth cooling, driven by anisotropic interfacial thermal stress from unidirectional Cu steps on vicinal Cu(111). The receiving nanoscrolls exhibit tunable thicknesses from 2 to 40 nm, and an approximately one-order-of-magnitude enhancement in photocurrent over planar monolayer graphene, together with improved conductance and carrier mobility. This process also enables the formation of adjacent wrinkle-free graphene single crystals, providing a promising strategy for wrinkle control in 2D materials. Rolled-up nanoscrolls based on 2D materials exhibit interesting emerging properties, but their scalable synthesis remains challenging. Here, the authors report the fabrication of aligned graphene nanoscrolls with tunable thickness via deterministic rolling of wafer-scale single-crystal graphene films during post-growth cooling, showing enhanced photoresponse and high carrier mobility.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting 10% of women, characterized by the growth of endometrial-like tissue outside the uterus. Through a genome-wide DNA methylation meta-analysis of nine independent cohorts ( n = 1138 samples), we show an epigenetic dichotomy: the eutopic endometrium of endometriosis cases shows no significant divergence from healthy controls, whereas ectopic lesions exhibit massive, consistent hyper/hypomethylation. We identify 1824 differentially methylated regions targeting the HOX clusters, ESR1 , and GATA2 , key regulators of cell differentiation and hormonal response. This suggests that endometriotic cells possess an epigenetic identity distinct from normal endometrial cells. While most alterations reflect biological mechanisms shared across anatomical sites, distinct signatures exist between lesion types. By harmonizing independent datasets, our study provides a high-resolution molecular map of lesions and strengthens the evidence that DNA methylation drives endometriosis biology.

candidates.abstract: Abstract The GID/CTLH ubiquitin ligase is a multisubunit E3 conserved across eukaryotes. GID/CTLH has been implicated in a variety of processes, including metabolic regulation, cell proliferation, embryonic development and cell differentiation. However, our understanding of substrate recognition by GID/CTLH remains incomplete. Here, we characterize the regulation, specificity and functions of the putative substrate receptor Gid11 in budding yeast. We find that upon its expression during the switch of carbon source from glucose to ethanol, Gid11 associates with the core GID complex, likely assembling into a ring-like complex. Through systematic mutagenesis, we identify a negatively charged pocket on Gid11 that binds substrates carrying N-terminal degrons starting with threonine and define the Thr/N-degron motif. Such Thr/N-degrons are exposed upon co-translational removal of the initiator methionine, while escaping N-terminal acetylation. Finally, we show that during the glucose-to-ethanol transition, GID Gid11 targets for degradation factors linked to ribosomal biogenesis, amino acid, nucleotide and central carbon metabolism, opposing the established role of GID during the reverse transition from ethanol to glucose. Taken together, our results establish Gid11 as a bona fide GID substrate receptor and highlight GID as a regulator of metabolic transitions.

candidates.title: Programmable synaptic and stochastic regimes in a monolayer hBN atomristor
candidates.authors: Yu-Rim Jeon, Sangheon Oh, Ebenezer C. Usih, Jeonghwan Kim, Chandan Biswas, Joseph S. Friedman, A. Alec Talin, Deji Akinwande
candidates.abstract: Electrically programmable control over distinct memristive operation regimes remains largely unexplored in atomically thin materials. Here we demonstrate a monolayer hBN atomristor in which electrical stimuli reversibly switch the device between synaptic and stochastic regimes within the same atomic-scale platform. Electrical, thermal, and low-frequency noise measurements across the HRS–LRS transition reveal regime-dependent signatures of localized Ag configuration in the monolayer hBN device. In the stochastic regime, stochastic fluctuations and switching probability are electrically programmable, whereas the synaptic regime exhibits stable potentiation and depression characteristics. System-level studies further show that the regime tunability can be exploited for both neuromorphic and probabilistic computing. These results establish electrically programmable dynamic regime control as an operational framework for atomically thin memristive systems, providing pathways towards reconfigurable energy-efficient computing hardware. 2D materials show rich dynamic behaviors, but most devices support only one operating regime. Jeon et al. report that a monolayer hBN memristor enables electrically programmable switching between synaptic and stochastic behaviors, providing distinct operating regimes within a single atomically thin device.

candidates.title: Diminished subsurface oxygen maximum linked to rapid decline of the North Pacific Central Mode Water
candidates.authors: Lixiao Xu, Jing Liu, Huishi Pan, Xiao-Tong Zheng, Zhaohui Chen, Sebastian Mieruch, Shang-Ping Xie, Bo Qiu, Angelicque E. White, James T. Potemra, David M. Karl, Fernando Santiago-Mandujano, Hu Yang, Xiaopei Lin, Junjie Xu
candidates.abstract: Mode waters strongly shape ocean heat storage and oxygen uptake, yet their persistence under continued warming remains unclear. Here we show a rapid decline in the North Pacific Central Mode Water (CMW) since the early 2020s, leading to a marked reduction in the subsurface oxygen maximum at Station ALOHA, the monitoring site for the Hawaii Ocean Time-series program, 50 km north of Oahu. In general, weakened westerlies over recent decades have intensified surface warming and stratification, suppressing CMW renewal, whereas strong El Niño typically strengthens the westerlies and promotes vigorous CMW formation. In contrast, we find that the strong 2023–2024 El Niño failed to reinvigorate the CMW because the El Niño–related atmospheric teleconnection pattern shifted unusually far east of the formation region. Similar atmospheric anomalies are projected under future warming scenarios, implying inhibited surface-thermocline exchanges due to failed mode water ventilation, with consequences for climate, biogeochemical cycles, and marine ecosystems. North Pacific Central Mode Water (CMW) shows a rapid decline from early 2020s, decreasing the subsurface oxygen maximum documented by Station ALOHA. Remarkably, the 2023–2024 El Niño failed to restore CMW due to atmospheric teleconnection.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Regulatory T (Treg) cells contribute to skin homeostasis, but the antigenic targets remain unclear. Whilst CD1a is known to present lipid antigens to effector T cells, the possibility of CD1a presentation to Treg cells us not fully understood. Here, we show CD1a reactivity in subsets of human circulating and cutaneous CD4 + Treg cells, displaying αβ T cell receptors (TCRs), memory phenotypes and suppressive functions, including the ability to secrete interleukin-10 (IL-10) in response to the permissive lipid antigen lysophosphatidylcholine, known to be enriched in skin inflammation. Moreover, CD1a-reactive IL-10-producing CD4 + Treg cells from patients with psoriasis up-regulate type 1 and type 17 pro-inflammatory signatures under in vitro stimulation, while a corresponding Treg cell population is enriched and dysfunctional in psoriatic lesions. Spatial transcriptomic analyses suggest that CD1a-reactive Treg cell signatures are localized in close proximity to CD1a⁺ antigen-presenting cells within psoriatic lesions and are potentially connected through ligand-receptor interactions relevant to cell-cell contact, recruitment, and functional regulation. Furthermore, clonally expanded IL-10-producing Treg cells retain their suppressive phenotype in a CD1a-dependent and TCR-dependent manner. Together, these findings show that subsets of Treg cells are directed to self-lipid antigens and CD1a, but show an altered phenotype equipped with pro-inflammatory potential in the setting of psoriasis.

candidates.title: Catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation for precise synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes
candidates.authors: Jingpeng Li, Guo Yang, Yilan Zhang, Meiqi Lin, Wenxuan Li, Shiang Li, Xinhui Lu, Tao Zeng, Wu-Qiang Wu, Zhenyu Yang
candidates.abstract: Organic semiconductors such as polythiophenes (PThs) offer substantial potential for flexible optoelectronics. Incorporating silicon into the PTh backbone represents a promising strategy to enhance flexibility and tune electronic properties; however, conventional metal-catalyzed synthetic approaches lack precise control over polymer chain growth, yielding materials with poorly defined energy levels and relatively board dispersity. Here, we report a catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation (TDP) strategy for the direct incorporation of silicon into PThs, producing a class of narrowly dispersed silicon-incorporated polymers. This thermally driven, radical-mediated mechanism circumvents the uncontrolled initiation and competitive pathways of conventional catalytic routes, enabling precise control over chain growth and yielding well-defined PThs with narrow dispersity (Đ = 1.2 – 1.4). The dehydrogenatively coupled diphenylsilane- terthiophene polymer (PS-1) shows favorable energy-level alignment and a hole mobility of 9.2 × 10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1. When employed as a hole-transport interlayer in inverted tin-lead (Sn-Pb) perovskite solar cells, PS-1 enables a champion power conversion efficiency of 23.3% with enhanced operational stability, surpassing the 20.8% efficiency of standard PEDOT:PSS-based devices. This work establishes a scalable synthetic route to advanced conjugated polymers, providing a versatile materials platform for optoelectronic applications. The synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes typically requires metal catalysts, which show poor polymerisation control and require post-synthesis purification. Here, the authors report a metal catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation strategy for the synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes with well defined structures, narrow dispersities and high charge carrier mobilities.

candidates.title: EcoVAE: a generative deep learning method for global species distribution prediction
candidates.authors: Yujing Yan, Bin Shao, Jiawei Yan, Charles C. Davis
candidates.abstract: Anthropogenic pressures on biodiversity necessitate efficient and scalable methods to predict global species distributions. Current species distribution models (SDMs) face challenges with large-scale datasets, complex species associations, and data quality. Here, we introduce EcoVAE, an autoencoder-based generative model that integrates bioclimatic variables with georeferenced occurrences. The model is trained separately for plants, butterflies, and mammals to predict global distributions at both genus and species levels. Through unsupervised learning, EcoVAE captures underlying distribution patterns from large-scale species occurrence data. It achieves high precision and speed, outperforming traditional SDMs in spatial block cross-validation. EcoVAE also reveals signatures of species associations that align with known prey-predator relationships. Taken together, these capacities enable the robust evaluation of global sampling efforts and interpolates distributions in data-limited regions, offering new applications for biodiversity exploration and monitoring. Predicting where species live is key to protecting biodiversity. The authors present EcoVAE, a generative model that rapidly and accurately predicts global species distributions, reveals species associations, and identifies sampling gaps.

candidates.title: Gut microbiota-derived phenylacetylglutamine exacerbates aortic aneurysm and dissection via activating macrophage integrin β1 in male mice
candidates.authors: Huanhuan Cao, Yanghui Chen, Xiaoyi Liu, Chenwei Lin, Qi Zhang, Jun Yang, Ke Li, Shusi Ding, Qiutong Wu, Jie Chen, Yiwen Fu, Xingxian Liu, Chao Jiang, Rui Zhan, Guangyuan Song, Lin Zeng, Zhe Zhao, Qing Wang, Xiaoyu Hu, Lixin Wang, Dao Wen Wang, Lemin Zheng
candidates.abstract: Abstract Aortic aneurysm and dissection (AAD) are life-threatening cardiovascular diseases with limited therapeutic options. It is essential to identify new risk factors and therapeutic targets for AAD. Recent evidence has highlighted the role of gut microbiota in AAD, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), a gut microbiota–derived metabolite, is associated with increased risk for AAD. Our study illustrates that elevated plasma PAGln levels were independently associated with increased AAD risk in a clinical cohort comprising 1,144 individuals. Exogenous PAGln supplementation exacerbated AAD in male mice, whereas AAV8-mediated hepatic knockdown of Glyat reduced circulating metabolite levels and ameliorated AAD. We further demonstrated that the elevated PAGln levels observed in disease are gut microbiota–dependent in origin. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that PAGln exacerbates AAD by expanding a pro-inflammatory IL6 (high) macrophage subpopulation. Mechanistically, PAGln directly binds to integrin α5β1 and downregulates the repressive H3K27me3 levels via the integrin α5β1–integrin-linked kinase (ILK)–lysine demethylase 6B (KDM6B) signaling, thereby enhancing IL6 transcriptional permissiveness. Genetic ablation of integrin β1, the receptor for PAGln, effectively ameliorated AAD in male mice. Our findings identify PAGln is associated with increased risk for AAD and reveal its potential as a therapeutic target.

candidates.title: A macrocyclic peptide inhibitor of the antibiotic transporter NorA
candidates.authors: Tiffany Suwatthee, Alex Nazzaro, Rupali Singh, Andrew I. Perault, Somrita Dey, Magdalena Podkowik, Priyanka Mishra, Kathryn Tao, Ganesh Jedhe, Huihui Kuang, Bo Shopsin, Paramjit S. Arora, Nathaniel J. Traaseth
candidates.abstract: Abstract Staphylococcus aureus is a human bacterial pathogen with an array of molecular mechanisms to evade the action of antibiotics. Within the organism, efflux pumps provide a first-line defense mechanism, enabling broad multidrug resistance across antibiotic classes and the ability for the organism to evolve target-level resistance mechanisms. NorA is a key efflux transporter in S. aureus responsible for conferring resistance to fluoroquinolones, puromycin, and other cytotoxic compounds. Here, we describe an approach to develop peptide efflux pump inhibitors (EPIs) of NorA by leveraging chemical synthesis and design, structure-based insights, and screening approaches to probe NorA pocket engagement and S. aureus growth inhibition. Our cryo-EM structure reveals that a lead peptide NPI-5 inserts deeply into NorA’s substrate binding pocket by using two tryptophan-arginine motifs to bind an anionic patch within NorA, thereby stabilizing the outward-facing conformation of the transporter and halting antibiotic efflux. Further optimization of NPI-5 involving unnatural residues and macrocyclization yielded cNPI-7, a peptide which potentiates fluoroquinolones in vitro and in a murine bacteremia infection model. The successful development of potent and selective peptide-based EPIs provides an approach for inhibiting other efflux systems from pathogenic organisms.

candidates.title: Cyclical high-magnitude lake drainage slows Greenland ice sheet motion
candidates.authors: Yefan Wang, Peter Nienow, Jaime Otero, Daniel N. Goldberg
candidates.abstract: Abstract Global glacier recession is driving a rapid increase in the number and volume of ice-marginal lakes, leading to more frequent Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). The long-term impact of GLOFs on glacier dynamics remains poorly understood, including in Greenland, which holds the largest glacial lake volume in the world. Here, using multi-decadal observations from Isortuarsuup Sermia, Southwest Greenland, we reveal that cyclical GLOFs regulate ice sheet motion. We identify a ‘sawtooth’ pattern of ice-dynamics, whereby multi-year acceleration is terminated abruptly by high-magnitude lake-drainage that resets the glacier to a ‘quiescent’ state for several years. The 2022 event exemplifies this process: the near-terminus ice velocity accelerated briefly from a pre-event baseline of ~200 m a −1 to ~1000 m a −1 before dropping to ~50 m a −1 over subsequent years. Each GLOF releases an immense meltwater volume (mean discharge in 2022 ~17000 m³ s −1 ), carving a ~1.5-km-wide, efficient subglacial channel. This channel enables extensive lowering of the subglacial water pressure, increasing ice–bed friction and suppressing ice motion. As climate warming increases GLOF frequency, this powerful negative feedback will modulate ice sheet motion acting as a brake on ice-dynamics at the margins of the Greenland Ice Sheet.

candidates.title: De novo identification of protein domains in cryo-electron tomography maps from AlphaFold2 models
candidates.authors: Yi Lu, Guanglin Chen, Fei Sun, Yun Zhu, Zhiyong Zhang
candidates.abstract: Sub-tomogram averaging of cryo-electron tomography maps often fails to reach the resolution required for atomic model building based on side-chain information, preventing accurate protein identification from the density alone. We develop DomainSeeker, which identifies protein domains by integrating AlphaFold2 models with experimental data. It partitions these models into domains by clique analysis of predicted aligned errors, fits them into segmented densities, and evaluates each fit globally and locally, deriving prior probabilities. Bayesian inference integrates the priors with cross-linking mass spectrometry, computing posterior probabilities. Applying prior probability analysis to mouse sperm microtubule doublet densities reveals higher recognition accuracy and resolution robustness than existing approaches. Incorporating cross-linking mass spectrometry for yeast nuclear pore complex densities further improves recognition performance and confidence. An interactive ChimeraX plugin facilitates user access. In this work, DomainSeeker addresses a bottleneck in in situ structural biology and supports visual proteomics in native cellular environments. Identifying proteins in medium- to low-resolution cryo-electron tomography density maps remains challenging. Here the authors develop DomainSeeker, which combines AlphaFold2 models with experimental data to identify protein domains from density maps.

candidates.title: A spectral-spatial interweaver for hyperdimensional photonic computing
candidates.authors: Yun-Long Nie, Hang Song, De-Hui Huang, Yi Xie, Chao-Qian Li, Yu-Xuan Fu, Yi-Xuan Chen, Xiao-Wen Shang, Feng Lu, Chao-Yang Zhang, Yu-Quan Peng, Chen-Ming Zhao, Chun-Yan Jin, Ya-Sen Yu, Chen-Shuo Xia, Yu-Lin Yu, Hai Yan, Yong-Xing Zhan, Jian-Peng Dou, Xiao-Yun Xu, Hao Tang, Xian-Min Jin
candidates.abstract: Photonic computing offers high bandwidth, parallelism and energy efficiency for artificial intelligence (AI), yet its scalability remains limited by bulky optical components and immature optoelectronic integration. Here we present HyperON, a thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) hyperdimensional optical network built around a passive spectral-spatial interweaver and broadband wavelength-parallel modulators. The interweaver combines wavelength multiplexing with spatial replication in a log2P-stage network, delivering the full wavelength set to every spatial output without beam-combination loss. By interweaving P spectral channels with K spatial units, HyperON forms a unified P × K parallel computing framework, supporting O(N2) operations with only O(N) modulators, improving hardware efficiency and scalability. A 16 × 16 interweaver shows low-loss, broadband and highly uniform operation across 1523.40-1568.85 nm, with 1.30 dB average loss, 0.196 dB output-port variation and 0.414 dB cross-wavelength variation. The integrated wavelength-parallel modulators retain system-level bandwidths of 53-67 GHz after large-scale routing, while standalone devices exhibit bandwidths beyond 67 GHz. Together, these features enable the fabricated HyperON chip to deliver a projected peak throughput of 32.8 TMAC/s, with estimated energy and area efficiencies of 7.04 TMAC/s/W and 0.163 TMAC/s/mm2, respectively. Experimental demonstrations in image convolution, handwritten digit recognition, and 64-mode parallel computing confirm its high speed operation, versatility, and scalability for large-scale AI workloads. Photonic computing promises faster, more energy-efficient AI, but hardware scaling remains challenging. Here, the authors present HyperON, a TFLN-based hyperdimensional photonic computing network combining a spectral-spatial interweaver with wavelength-parallel modulators.

candidates.title: 3D-MINSTED nanoscopy and protein tracking in densely labelled living cells
candidates.authors: Julius Bernhard Peters, Christopher Heidebrecht, Michael Weber, Marcel Leutenegger, Stefan W. Hell
candidates.abstract: Abstract Investigating the movements and conformational changes of proteins in living cells is essential for understanding their function. The recently introduced fluorescence nanoscopy method called MINSTED has successfully tracked single fluorophore-labelled proteins, albeit in fixed cells and two dimensions only. Here we introduce a MINSTED setup for live-cell tracking of individual proteins in three dimensions (3D) with a localization precision σ down to <1 nm. Applied to the motor protein kinesin-1, our MINSTED nanoscope follows single proteins in 3D as they process along microtubules in 16 nm steps. Individual steps are resolved amid substantial intracellular background. The unique capability of the 3D stimulated emission depletion (STED) beam to carve out the signal of the protein label of interest enables efficient single-molecule investigations at hitherto unpractically high concentrations of labelled proteins and thus in crowded live-cell environments.

candidates.title: Autosomal dosage compensation in aneuploidy and cancer involves transcriptional burst regulation
candidates.authors: Natali Papanicolaou, Sebastian Wettersten, Guilherme Maia, Antonio Lentini, Björn Reinius
candidates.abstract: Abstract Aneuploidy, resulting from whole-chromosome or segmental gains and losses, is generally detrimental to organismal fitness and is strongly associated with tumorigenesis. While sex chromosome aneuploidies are relatively well tolerated due to dedicated allelic dosage compensation mechanisms, the existence of comparable regulatory processes for autosomes remains debated. Here, we investigate transcriptional responses to autosomal aneuploidy and identify widespread dosage compensation across affected chromosomes. Using high-sensitivity allele-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing of monoclonal cell expansions spanning diverse ploidies and degrees of aneuploidy, we uncover consistent transcriptional compensation of both chromosomal gains and losses. This response operates in a region-specific manner across both complete and segmental aneuploidies, revealing an unexpected flexibility in dosage regulation. We show that chromosome losses are compensated through increased transcriptional burst frequency from the remaining allele. Complementary proteomics analyses demonstrate additional buffering at the protein level, resulting in a substantial, though still incomplete, restoration of stoichiometric balance across autosomal aneuploid chromosomes for both copy number gains and losses. Analyses of cancer transcriptomes confirm that compensatory mechanisms are active in human tumours. Together, our findings establish dosage compensation as a genome-wide and dynamic response to gene dose imbalance. This mechanism extends beyond sex chromosomes, supports transcriptional homeostasis, and represents a fundamental and evolutionarily conserved mode of gene regulation active across species and in aneuploid cancer cells.

candidates.abstract: CD33 is associated with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) susceptibility. The AD-associated rs3865444C risk variant reduces splicing of the sialic acid-binding domain, increasing the sialic acid-binding isoform seven-fold. Here we identify CD45, a GWAS-associated AD risk gene, as an immune cell-specific sialic acid-dependent cis CD33 binding partner, whose phosphatase activity CD33 inhibits. CD33 loss improved microglial amyloid beta clearance and protected against amyloid beta-induced dendritic spine loss in microglial-neuronal co-cultures, whereas CD45 loss impaired clearance, aligning with detrimental effects of CD33-mediated CD45 inhibition. CD33-CD45 interaction frequency was increased in monocytes from rs3865444CC individuals versus rs3865444AA, as well as in AD versus controls, independent of genotype. An interaction between CD33 and PTPRC (CD45) expression in human brain tissue was associated with a pathological AD diagnosis and global burden of AD pathology, consistent with the cellular findings above. Together, our results link CD33-mediated suppression of CD45 with AD genetic susceptibility and systemic myeloid dysfunction. CD33 and CD45 are both genetically linked to Alzheimer’s risk. Here the authors show the two proteins physically interact, and this interaction is increased in Alzheimer’s disease.

candidates.abstract: Human chromosome 15q13.3 is a hotspot for recurrent pathogenic copy number variants (CNVs) associated with schizophrenia, developmental delay and epilepsy. We generated long-read genome assemblies for 10 patient-parent trios and compared them to 581 population control haplotypes from diverse ancestry where this complex region is fully resolved. We find that both the long (“BP4-BP5”) and short (“CHRNA7”) forms of 15q13.3 CNVs arise predominantly by non-allelic homologous recombination (NAHR) whose susceptibility has been promoted by large inversion polymorphisms. While three BP4-BP5 breakpoints cluster in a 2 kbp PRDM9-enriched recombination hotspot, most CNVs are structurally distinct and affect the disease-relevant genes ARHGAP11B and CHRFAM7A differentially. Population analyses reveal at least 18 distinct structural haplotypes in 15q13.3 and show that the risk for BP4-BP5 CNVs is stratified more than 10-fold depending on ancestry, with 68.4% of Europeans but only 5.1% of East Asians predisposed, establishing inversion polymorphisms as major determinants of population-specific recurrent CNV susceptibility. Comparison to six ape species indicates that the duplication architecture promoting instability expanded recently and is largely human-specific. Recurrent copy-number variants at chromosome 15q13.3 cause neurodevelopmental disorders. Using long-read genome assemblies the authors show that these events arise via recombination promoted by inversions that vary in frequency across populations.

candidates.title: Orbit-Qubit Quantum Processor of Ultracold Atoms
candidates.authors: Ming-Gen He, Wei-Yong Zhang, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, Jian-Wei Pan
candidates.abstract: It is challenging to build scalable quantum processors capable of both parallel control and local operation. As a promising platform to overcome this challenge, optical lattices offer exceptional parallelism. However, it has been struggling with precise local operations due to relatively narrow lattice spacings. Here, we introduce a new quantum processor incorporating orbit-qubit encoding and internal states (as auxiliary degrees of freedom) to achieve spatially selective operations together with parallel control. With this processor, we generate one-dimensional and two-dimensional cluster states using minimal layers of controlled-Z gates. We experimentally detect the multipartite entanglement of a two-dimensional cluster state involving 123 orbit qubits through direct stabilizer measurements, verifying the full bipartite non-separability. Furthermore, we demonstrate measurement-based quantum computation by implementing single-qubit and two-qubit logical gates, highlighting the flexibility of orbit-qubit operations. Our results establish orbit-qubit optical lattices as a scalable quantum processing architecture, opening new pathways for quantum computation applications.

candidates.title: Are Pulsar Timing Array Measurements Sensitive to Gravitational Wave Non-Gaussianities?
candidates.authors: Chiara Cecchini, Jonas El Gammal, Gabriele Franciolini, Mauro Pieroni
candidates.abstract: Observing non-Gaussianities in the timing residuals of pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) has recently attracted attention as a potential discriminator between astrophysical and cosmological origins of the observed gravitational wave (GW) signal. In this Letter, we show that, even in an idealized signal-dominated setup, after decorrelating the data to avoid spurious detections, statistical tests applied to PTA data cannot distinguish between a Gaussian and a non-Gaussian amplitude distribution of the GW background in a model-agnostic way. In particular, without making strong assumptions on the GW spectrum or the properties of the population, the sensitivity to any distinctive non-Gaussian feature is washed out.

candidates.abstract: Inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments at the National Ignition Facility (NIF) use high-density carbon shells doped with low-concentration tungsten in a thin, uniform-density, buried layer, to suppress deleterious high-energy x-ray pre-heating. Recent radiation-hydrodynamics simulations suggest that this boxcar dopant-concentration profile causes hydrodynamically unstable density gradients leading to fuel-shell mixing and up to 2× degraded neutron yields. To address this, a new ramped profile was tested, where the dopant concentration linearly ramps up and back down. Two NIF experiments using this strategy demonstrated neutron yield improvements of up to 2.2× over the closest boxcar comparison, achieving a record 8.6 MJ yield, 20.1 keV hot-spot temperature, and a target gain of 4.1. These results show that ramped doping is consistent with mitigation of fuel-ablator mixing and marks a key development for ICF science.

candidates.title: Probing the Memory of a Superconducting Qubit Environment
candidates.authors: Nicolas Gosling, Denis Bénâtre, Paul Kugler, Simon Geisert, Nicolas Zapata, Mitchell Field, Sumeru Hazra, Simon Günzler, Thomas Reisinger, Martin Spiecker, Mathieu Féchant, Ioan M. Pop
candidates.abstract: Achieving fault tolerance with superconducting quantum processors requires qubits to operate within the regime of threshold theorems based on the Born-Markov approximation. This approximation, which models dissipation as constant energy decay into a memoryless environment, breaks down when qubits couple to long-lived two-level systems (TLSs) that become polarized during operation and retain memory of past qubit states. Here, we show that non-Poissonian quantum jump traces carry the information required to distinguish long-lived TLSs from the standard Markovian bath. By fitting the Solomon equations to measured quantum jump dynamics arising naturally from thermal fluctuations, we can disentangle the qubit’s coupling to the two environments. Sweeping the qubit frequency reveals distinct peaks, each associated with a TLS that outlives the qubit, providing a handle to understand their microscopic origin.

candidates.authors: P. J. Bilbao, T. Silva, L. O. Silva
candidates.abstract: Plasma-based accelerators are beginning to employ relativistic beams with unprecedented charge and ultrashort durations. These dense driver beams can drive wakes even in high-density plasmas ( ≳ 10 19 cm − 3 ), where betatron radiation becomes increasingly important and begins to affect the dynamics of the accelerated beam. We show that betatron cooling leads to a strong structuring of the phase space of the beam. This gives rise to bunched, ring-like structures with positive radial position and momentum gradients, i.e., population inversion of the amplitude of oscillation. We derive the characteristic timescales for this process analytically and confirm our predictions with multidimensional particle-in-cell simulations. The radiation-dominated regime of beam dynamics fundamentally alters the acceleration process and produces self-structured beams; particle-in-cell simulations of the resulting beams show that it becomes unstable to the ion-channel laser and lead to exponential amplification of radiation.

candidates.title: High-Purity Entanglement Mediated by Magnons Despite Weak Coupling
candidates.authors: Sanchar Sharma
candidates.abstract: Entangling distant spins via a shared magnonic bus typically faces a tradeoff: stronger spin-magnon coupling increases the entanglement fidelity, but also the spin decay rate. We propose a protocol that breaks this tradeoff. The magnons couple only to a transition outside the computational basis, in which the Bell state is created. Our protocol is probabilistic, and weak coupling mainly reduces the success probability, with only a small effect on the fidelity. We analyze a setup where the spins are two nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers near a magnetic wire. In the absence of NV dephasing, the protocol reaches unit fidelity with a maximally entangled state, for arbitrarily weak coupling. In our simulations via the Monte-Carlo wavefunction approach, the NV-magnon coupling is taken to be one-third of the magnon linewidth. Considering finite NV dephasing, we predict a fidelity of > 0.99 for a state-of-the-art rate, and an optimal fidelity of 0.91 for a moderate rate, both at 0.6 % success probability.

candidates.abstract: Complex networks of biochemical reactions have been proposed to exhibit emergent cooperativity that can be described by an effective Ising model, with a small number of parameters encoding collective interactions. Here this mapping is experimentally tested using the response of three bacterial species to a range of antibiotics acting on different cellular targets. The Ising description is compared to the conventional Hill model, examining both the mean growth-rate response and, importantly, its population growth-rate heterogeneity (PGRH). While both models describe the mean growth-rate dependence on antibiotic concentration comparably well, we find that the Ising model provides a markedly better description of PGRH, offering an additional and more stringent test of the collective description. The fitted Ising interaction strength is systematically related to the Hill exponent and increases with the functional distance of the antibiotic target from the protein-production machinery. These results provide experimental support for describing complex biochemical reaction networks through effective cooperative Ising interactions, and suggest that the collective response of bacterial growth to antibiotics reflects the organization of the underlying metabolic network.

candidates.abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is commonly viewed through two limiting regimes: strongly correlated flat bands near the magic angle and nearly decoupled Dirac cones at large twist angles. Here we explore the intermediate regime. Using hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons (HP$^{3}$) to probe the dynamical electronic response, we investigate bilayer graphene from AB stacking to $5.5^\circ$ TBG. We identify a narrow density window in which the HP$^{3}$ wavelength becomes strongly gate tunable. The window opens when doping suppresses Landau damping and a coherent graphene plasmon emerges. It closes at a second crossover, which appears only above $4^\circ$ and shifts systematically with twist angle. Continuum-model and electrodynamic calculations trace this second crossover to hybridization between the central and remote moiré bands, which weakens the density dependence of the Drude response. The resulting polaritonic tunability is concentrated within a twist-angle-selected density window and produces total wavelength changes approaching $90\%$. Our results demonstrate that remote moiré bands reshape the collective electrodynamics of TBG far from the magic-angle regime and establish large-angle TBG as a platform for gate-reconfigurable mid-infrared polaritons and material cavities.

candidates.abstract: Competing interactions can generate frustration which suppresses macroscopic-scale phase separation, superseding it with separation patterns on the microscopic scale. This phenomenon, referred to as microphase separation, produces thermodynamically stable mesoscopic-scale periodic patterns in systems of different physical nature. The studies of this effect follow two paradigms. First, in block copolymers, the macroscopic-scale separation of chemically distinct components is prevented by the covalent bonds between them. In the other, the microscopic-scale separation is produced in simple single-component liquids by the competition between a short-range attraction and a long-range repulsion (SALR) in the pair potential, the separation occurring between a dense phase and a gas. The interest in the simple liquid models with SALR interaction was inspired by the apparent universality of the modulated structures generated by competing interactions in different systems. Simple particle models are tractable by theory and thereby make it possible to discern the microscopic mechanisms of pattern formation; particle-based simulations give access to systems beyond the reach of experiments. In this Perspective we review the recent advances in the molecular-dynamics simulation of microphase separation in single-component simple liquids using SALR potentials. We show that these simulations reproduce the mesophases typical of block copolymers and liquid crystals, which demonstrates that the complexity of the constituent particles of real liquids is not a necessary condition for their formation, and that they produce novel periodic morphologies of both conceptual interest and technological relevance; we discuss how simulated mesophases can serve as templates for metamaterials whose properties are governed by topology.

candidates.abstract: Atomically dispersed catalysts exhibit molecule-solid crossover character when localized metal orbitals hybridize with support-derived bands, a regime not fully captured by either a d-band-center description or a frontier-orbital picture. We establish an electronic-to-geometric framework for oxygen reduction across fourteen metals. N-to-P substitution in M-N4 sites raises theoretical onset potentials in 13 systems, with Rh-N3P reaching 0.88 V, comparable to the Pt(111) benchmark. Scaling relations reduce *OOH, *O, and *OH thermodynamics to $Δ$G*OH. M-N4 follows a dyz-dominated frontier-orbital picture, whereas M-N3P requires a weighted frontier d-state representation built from adsorption-relevant orbitals and their occupancies. The resulting $ε$WFDS correlates with $Δ$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.92, compared with 0.83 for the d-band center and 0.64 for the frontier-orbital. The identified roles of orbital occupancy and local coordination suggest an interpretable geometric descriptor, $ζ$M-N3P = nd/rM-P, that predicts $Δ$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.96. The ORR volcano analysis identifies strong-binding systems and motivates axial oxygen coordination. This design raises onset potentials by 0.70-2.46 V, and the M-N3PO descriptor predicts $Δ$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.91. By bridging frontier-orbital and d-band-center descriptions, the framework provides a physically grounded electronic representation and a geometry-based screening route compatible with machine-learned interatomic potentials.

candidates.abstract: Optical excitation offers a contact-free, ultrafast route to charge and spin currents, with symmetry determining which nonlinear photocurrents are allowed and whether they carry charge, spin, or both. Spin-group symmetry describes the limit without spin-orbit coupling (SOC), whereas magnetic-group symmetry accounts for SOC. We show that the two descriptions yield different selection rules for both charge and spin photocurrents in the multiferroic compensated ferrimagnet GaFeO$_3$. Without SOC, only linear shift and circular injection currents are allowed, with identical components for charge and spin, so every charge current is spin polarized along the moments. SOC leaves these charge currents nearly unchanged, activates magnetic linear injection and circular shift charge currents, and enables pure spin currents polarized perpendicular to the moments. Ferroelectric switching reverses the linear shift and circular injection charge currents and their spin polarization. These findings establish the importance of magnetic-group symmetry for a complete description of nonlinear charge and spin photocurrents in compensated ferrimagnets.

candidates.abstract: We extend our previously introduced mean-field bond model from unary fcc lattices to crystals with multiple chemical species and sublattices, accurately predicting finite-temperature thermodynamics without statistical sampling. Our generalization reformulates the model in terms of the Wyckoff positions of the crystal, representing each by one atom, and solving for the bond density of the reference bond of each of its neighbor shells. Bond-bond correlation functions are built from the zero-temperature force constants, allowing the deviation of every bond in the crystal to be expressed through linear functions of the reference bond of a shell. Thermodynamic self-consistency is enforced by requiring a single virial temperature for the whole crystal, and compatibility of average bond lengths with crystal volume. Model predictions are validated against molecular dynamics simulations of unary, binary, and ternary crystals using Morse-type bonding potentials, parametrized for each shell from the force constants of empirical interatomic potentials at several isotropic strains. In each case, the predicted bond densities and thermodynamics agree with the simulations to within their statistical uncertainty. We discuss strategies for combining the model with bonding potentials parametrized from first principles and foundation models to predict the finite-temperature thermodynamics of complex crystals at ab initio accuracy without statistical sampling.

candidates.abstract: The electrical degradation and time-dependent current behavior of vertical $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) subjected to energetic Au-ion irradiation were systematically investigated. Two successive irradiation exposures were conducted under a constant reverse bias of $-100$ V to evaluate the effects of heavy-ion irradiation on device performance and transient current response. Following irradiation, the devices exhibited degraded forward conduction, increased specific on-resistance, enhanced reverse leakage current, and reduced apparent carrier concentration. During irradiation, pronounced increases in leakage current and transient current spikes were observed. Following each beam termination, the leakage current exhibited an initial rapid decay followed by a slower relaxation process. Single-exponential fitting identified distinct fast and slow relaxation components, while a double-exponential model provided a more comprehensive description of the overall current decay. After the second irradiation exposure, the characteristic time constants of the fast and slow relaxation processes increased from 33.50 to 40.64 s and from 190.35 to 282.29 s, respectively, indicating prolonged recovery dynamics under repeated irradiation. A charge-trapping-based model is proposed to explain the irradiation-induced current enhancement and subsequent fast and slow relaxation processes through modulation and gradual recovery of the effective Schottky tunneling barrier. These findings provide insights into the relationship between heavy-ion-induced electrical degradation and time-dependent current relaxation in $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ SBDs.

candidates.abstract: We present a framework for building and benchmarking scalable machine learning (ML) models based on simulating free-fermion systems. Our fermionic ML (FermiML) framework is (i) versatile enough to encompass kernel methods and neural networks, (ii) applicable to classification and regression, and (iii) scalable to real-world datasets. FermiML models are quantum circuits sharing the building blocks of most quantum ML (QML) models: (parameterized) qubit rotations and entangling gates. This allows us to build fermionic surrogates that mimic the architecture, and hence the quantum resources and inductive bias, of any QML model while remaining efficiently classically simulable. We thus benchmark QML models against close fermionic counterparts on equal footing and ascertain whether a purported QML gain truly stems from classically inaccessible resources or is an accidental side-effect. Across 31 configurations from five classification datasets, we benchmark quantum kitchen sinks (QKS), instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) and generic parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) models against fermionic surrogates. fQKS significantly outperforms QKS and is statistically indistinguishable from IQP and PQC; fPQC outperforms IQP and QKS and ties PQC in 28 configurations. We also introduce fermionic fidelity and Pfaffian covariance kernels for regression and establish QML baselines for this harder task. Finally, we introduce a fermionic energy-based classifier scalable to large text and image datasets, which outperforms prominent QML models on images, beats or closely trails them on text, and stays close to classical baselines throughout. Our results show that while performance depends sensitively on architecture, FermiML yields fermionic surrogates that challenge or outperform their unrestricted counterparts and fermionic QML models that match the scale of classical baselines on real-world datasets.

candidates.abstract: The spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice in a magnetic field is a paradigmatic frustrated quantum magnet, yet its ground-state phase diagram at generic anisotropy and its thermal phase structure remain incompletely understood. Here, using infinite density-matrix renormalization group, infinite projected entangled-pair operator, and exponential tensor renormalization group methods, supported by exact diagonalization, we resolve both issues. At zero temperature, we map the phase diagram continuously from the Ising limit to the Heisenberg point and find that the nonclassical $Ψ$ supersolid is a stable phase just below saturation at all anisotropies studied: it borders the one-third-magnetization up-up-down plateau directly in the strongly easy-axis regime and the semiclassical $V$ phase toward the Heisenberg point. In the strongly easy-axis regime, we uncover an intrinsically finite-temperature bond-nematic phase above the zero-temperature plateau--$Ψ$ boundary, in which the three bond directions become spontaneously inequivalent without transverse spin coherence or three-sublattice order. A hard-core-boson mapping reveals its origin: once thermal fluctuations destroy phase coherence, the field-doped holes settle on domain walls of the local up-up-down order, which are stabilized by quantum kink delocalization and aligned by its $Z_3$ registry. Our results call for reexamining high-field states in triangular-lattice cobaltates such as Na$_2$BaCo(PO$_4$)$_2$ and K$_2$Co(SeO$_3$)$_2$.

candidates.abstract: Spatially nonlocal symmetries need not imply nonlocal gauge dynamics. Nonlocal canonical transformations make certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions onsite while retaining sufficient Hamiltonian locality for gauging. Symmetry relocalization yields exact or emergent gauge locality in 1D, 2D, and 3D, subject to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies. In 1D, a Hamiltonian-preserving transformation exchanges onsite vector and nonlocal spectral axial charges of a half-filled chain, enabling local gauging of each and exposing their mixed anomaly. Bosonization identifies momentum-winding T-duality, with a parity-projected operator flowing to a noninvertible topological defect. A nonperturbative norm-resolvent bound proves emergent dynamical gauge locality at finite chemical potential, while a doubled Chern-insulator parent reveals the duality's bulk origin and superconducting extensions reveal hidden compact symmetries. In 2D, the square $π$-flux Majorana model shares the Kitaev honeycomb model's single Dirac fermion and odd Pfaffian parity but supports sharp and exponentially local compact charges, the latter with nontrivial Chern topology. Relocalization retains Schwartz locality for asymptotically local gauging, while AIII/AII parents clarify bulk charge origin and parity-anomaly inflow. Two flavors yield compact $U(2)$, a quaternionic invariant, and asymptotically local non-Abelian gauging. In 3D, an exact mixed vector-axial flux response is derived, while a distinct model supports an exponentially local vector $U(1)$ charge with strong quaternionic topology. A nonlocal map makes the charge and Kramers symmetry onsite while preserving exponential Hamiltonian locality. For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.

The stochastic forcing is represented by a Karhunen--Loève series and embedded into an autonomous, augmented phase space using a harmonic auxiliary phase. This representation allows us to construct the ERT dissipation function for fixed mode amplitudes and recover stochastic averages by averaging over the amplitudes and the initial phase. For the variance, we derive the response at finite spectral truncation and show analytically that, with uniform phase sampling, the full-spectrum white-noise limit reproduces the generator-based result for a sudden temperature change. Furthermore, a comparison with first-order linear response theory highlights how this may fail in general. In particular, if the noise-induced variance is quadratic in the noise amplitude, it is completely omitted by linear response. The analysis provides a framework for this model and for studying more general forcing; extensions to non-Markovian dynamics require separate convergence and regularity analyses.

candidates.abstract: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom. In time-dependent density functional theory on lattices, we show that not every ground state of a connected lattice can serve as the initial state of the density-potential map. A counterexample is the ground state of two fermions on a square that Penz and van Leeuwen found as a counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem. For almost every static potential, however, every real ground state can serve as an initial state, also for spin-resolved densities. We also give formal proofs that the time-dependent Kohn-Sham potential exists, locally in time, for almost every static Kohn-Sham potential, and of known results: local existence and uniqueness of the time-dependent potential for an admissible initial state, continuation in time up to the boundary of the set of admissible states, and the convergence properties of a regularized Kohn-Sham iteration. All theorems and propositions are formalized in the proof assistant Lean 4 and checked by computer.

candidates.abstract: Electron-phonon coupling (EPC) plays a vital role in the electrical and optical properties of materials, ranging from superconductivity to charge dynamics. In moiré superlattices, out-of-plane vibrations can modulate the moiré potential and enhance interlayer EPC. Here we report the first direct observation of a resonance arising from coupling between moiré electronic excitations and phonons in graphene-based moiré superlattices. Using Fourier-transform infrared photocurrent spectroscopy, we detect the nominally silent hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) out-of-plane optical (ZO) phonon as a pronounced absorption peak. The phonon interferes with moiré flat-band excitations to form a characteristic Fano resonance. Displacement field-dependent measurements confirm that the feature originates from coupling to the moiré electronic continuum rather than simple zone folding. We further observe similar resonances in devices with different graphene layer numbers and twist configurations. This enhanced EPC provides a pathway for understanding and controlling emerging quantum phenomena, such as superconductivity, and engineering novel optoelectronic devices.

candidates.abstract: Equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) achieve near-quantum-chemical accuracy, but their computational cost and GPU memory footprint restrict molecular dynamics (MD) at extended length and time scales. Even when the tensor product (TP) is accelerated, both bottlenecks remain governed by evaluating and storing per-edge radial weights in the NequIP convolution. We introduce JET-MLIPs (Joint-Kernel Equivariant Convolution with Tabulated Radial Weights for MLIP simulation), a GPU backend applicable to pretrained NequIP-family potentials without retraining. JET-MLIPs replaces the radial multilayer perceptron (MLP) with a piecewise cubic Hermite table and fuses table lookup, spherical harmonics, TP and neighbor aggregation into a single kernel, eliminating per-edge radial-weight and MLP-intermediate storage during force evaluation. Across 15 released potentials from SevenNet, MACE, NequIP-OAM, Nequix and EquFlash on a 5632-atom liquid electrolyte, LAMMPS MD attains 1.5-5.9$\times$ step-time speed-ups and 2.4-24$\times$ peak memory reductions relative to each family's existing TP-accelerated backend on a single H200 GPU while preserving single-precision (fp32) accuracy and dynamical stability. These reductions enable multi-nanosecond transport-property simulations of roughly $10^4$-atom systems on a single GPU and broaden access to large-scale equivariant MLIP MD on widely available GPUs.

candidates.abstract: The stability of ground states in the Edwards-Anderson Ising spin glass in dimensions two and higher against perturbations of a single coupling can be quantified through the ``flexibility'' of that coupling in a particular ground state. The property of $σ$-criticality is one in which varying a single coupling can alter the flexibilities of a (strictly) positive density of couplings in an infinite system, and its presence provides a sufficient condition for the presence of multiple ground state pairs. In a previous paper it was shown for the EA spin glass that $σ$-criticality of the first kind, in which the critical droplet of a bond has a positive-density interface with the ground state, was ruled out in any dimension. The remaining possibility, called $σ$-criticality of the second kind, is one in which a bond lies in the critical droplet boundaries of a positive density of other bonds. We show here that this kind of $σ$-criticality is also absent, ruling out altogether the presence of $σ$-criticality in the EA spin glass. While this doesn't resolve the question of multiplicity of ground state pairs, it removes a sufficient condition for its presence. We then propose a rigorous necessary condition for ground state pair multiplicity.

candidates.abstract: We present a numerical workflow for the reduced BCS Richardson model, combining the eigenvalue-based Bethe equations, Baxter-polynomial reconstruction, and complex root finding. Newton-Raphson iteration solves the nonlinear equations for the eigenvalue-based variables; a linear system yields the polynomial coefficients, and Laguerre iteration with polynomial deflation extracts the rapidities. We apply the procedure to equally spaced, quadratic, and hydrogen-like non-degenerate single-particle spectra as the pairing strength varies. For finite systems, we calculate canonical observables from the complete seniority-zero spectrum and check benchmark spectra against exact diagonalization. In an eight-level, four-pair system with a hydrogen-like spectrum, the heat capacity has two maxima at weak coupling. With increasing coupling, the low-temperature maximum shifts upward and the high-temperature maximum downward; the latter ceases to be a distinct local maximum near $g\simeq0.03515$ in the units used. The equally spaced benchmark instead has a single dominant maximum over the coupling interval displayed for that spectrum. This comparison illustrates how single-particle level spacings can shape finite-size thermal response. The C++ code is publicly available; numerical instabilities remain possible near ill-conditioned configurations and at larger sizes.

candidates.abstract: As a mesoscopic diffusive wire at low temperatures is driven out of equilibrium by a current, excess noise is observed compared to the equilibrium Johnson-Nyquist fluctuations. The expected form of the excess noise varies depending on the relative rates of wire traversal, electron-electron inelastic energy transfer, and electron-phonon inelastic energy transfer. In long wires, the simple model of electron-phonon energy loss known to be quantitatively effective below a few Kelvin underpredicts the excess noise in the high bias, high temperature limit. This issue is more severe in wires on SiO2/Si than on bare Si, implying that interfacial thermal conduction must be considered in the thermal path even at comparatively high temperatures.

candidates.abstract: The celebrated Aubry-André-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-André-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.

candidates.abstract: We study the superconducting response induced by a Néel domain wall in a thin superconducting film proximity-coupled to a ferromagnetic layer in the presence of interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The combined action of the magnetic texture and broken inversion symmetry generates a magnetoelectric coupling that induces spontaneous equilibrium currents. To establish the basic response to a continuously rotating magnetic texture, we first consider a periodic harmonic cycloid as an analytically tractable reference problem. Near Tc, this reference problem illustrates how the magnetoelectric coupling modifies the superconducting order parameter, while below Tc it provides a simple setting for describing the phase response, Pearl screening, and the interaction with a vortex. We then turn to the main problem of this work, a single Néel domain wall, and derive analytical expressions for its equilibrium phase profile, spontaneous current, magnetic field, and vortex-wall interaction energy.We show that the Néel wall acts as an extended magnetoelectric source and produces a vorticity-selective pinning landscape controlled by the competition between the wall width and the effective screening length. We further demonstrate that sufficiently strong magnetoelectric coupling can render a bound vortex-antivortex pair energetically favorable relative to the vortex-free state, even in the absence of an applied magnetic field. Our results provide an analytical framework for understanding magnetoelectric vortex pinning and vortex-antivortex nucleation by Néel domain walls in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films.

candidates.abstract: Spin-logic devices promise non-volatile logic-in-memory computing with ultra-low power consumption, offering a route to circumvent the von Neumann bottleneck. Magnetoelectric and ferroelectric spin-orbit (MESO/FESO) devices, however, require spin-charge interconversion materials that combine a large output signal with properties that survive nanoscale integration. Tellurides are particularly fragile in this respect, as processing readily introduces defects that degrade their spin-charge interconversion properties. Here we demonstrate room-temperature spin-charge interconversion in patterned FESO nanoscale devices based on sputtered GeTe, with feature sizes down to 100 nm. By introducing a Ti interfacial layer between the CoFe electrode and GeTe, and by using GeTe films of improved crystalline quality, we increase the interconversion output signal from 3 mΩ to 24 mΩ, exceeding values reported for platinum at comparable device size. These results establish large-scale-deposited GeTe as a viable material platform for spin-logic devices and identify interface quality and film crystallinity as key levers for optimizing their performance.

candidates.abstract: We study the spectrum of arrays of critical transverse field Ising chains perturbed by a weak inter-chain coupling in the scaling limit, using an exact diagonalization algorithm based on Hamiltonian truncation. As the number of chains is made large, we confirm the existence of excitations below the two particle continuum that can be identified with the celebrated Zamalodchikov $E_8$ theory with small corrections. In addition, we find a distinct $ψ$-particle, with mass $M_\mathrmψ$ which is not contained in the $E_8$ theory. Its ratio to the lowest $E_8$ mass ($M_1$) is a universal number, which we have computed numerically to be $M_\mathrmψ/M_1 = 1.819\cdots$ for a one dimensional array of critical chains. We present evidence that this new state fundamentally involves excitations on neighboring chains, explaining why it has no analogue in the single chain problem. Interestingly the $M_\mathrmψ$ mass has a characteristic scaling dependence on detuning from the critical point that is qualitatively distinct from the $E_8$ masses, which can help identify it in spectroscopic experiments on easy-axis magnetic chain materials.

candidates.abstract: A perpendicular electric field can reorient a momentum-space spin texture without changing the local magnetic configuration. In this Letter, we investigate this mechanism in a $21^\circ$-twisted $\mathrm{NiPS}_3$ bilayer with zigzag order and coplanar, nonparallel layer Néel vectors. In the ideal nonrelativistic limit, an antiunitary in-plane half-translation enforces opposite-spin pairing at opposite momenta, while a layer-exchanging twofold operation pins the leading $p$-wave spin splitting to a crystallographic direction. A perpendicular layer bias lifts this orientational constraint while preserving the antiunitary symmetry, allowing a transverse component of the splitting vector. First-principles calculations show gate-dependent reorientation and deformation of spin-resolved isoenergy contours. Wannier-based linear-response calculations further reveal field-activated diagonal spin conductivities and a polarity-dependent tilt in the angular profile of the transverse spin-current response. The spin-texture axis, dispersion axes, and transport-response axis are distinct quantities governed by the same symmetry reduction. These results identify layer bias as a route to controlling odd-parity spin textures and spin-current anisotropy, provided that the coplanar magnetic state remains stable.

candidates.abstract: The Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon states bound to a vortex line in a clean type-II superconductor form one-dimensional minibands that disperse along the vortex. The lowest miniband is separated from the Fermi level by a minigap $E_0\simΔ^2/E_F$. A magnetic field shifts the minibands of the two spin projections in opposite directions. At the threshold field $B^*$ the Zeeman energy equals $E_0$. Estimates for FeSe place $B^*$ at a few tesla. The lowest miniband of one spin projection then crosses the Fermi level, and a spin-polarized one-dimensional Fermi sea forms inside the vortex core. We develop the theory of tunneling spectra across this Lifshitz transition. We solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations numerically in the quantum limit for all momenta along the vortex and compute the local density of states with thermal and instrumental broadening. The zero-bias conductance at the vortex center is absent below $B^*$. It has a maximum near $B^*$ with the inverse-square-root field dependence of a one-dimensional van Hove singularity and decreases at higher fields. The next miniband produces a second onset at a finite distance from the center. The zero-bias signal is carried by one spin projection at the center and by the opposite one in the surrounding ring. We then project the screened electron interaction onto the filled miniband. The resulting Luttinger parameter is close to unity, so the core hosts a weakly interacting one-dimensional Fermi gas. Its quasiparticles relax through three-particle collisions in analogy with thermalization in quantum wires and at quantum Hall edges. The corresponding relaxation rates are established analytically.
